cim: Mexican and Chinese Universities Expand AI and R&D Cooperation
cim_eredeti: Mexican and Chinese Universities Expand AI and R&D Cooperation
szoveg_eredeti:
Universities from Mexico and China agreed to expand bilateral cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI), applied research, student mobility, and mutual degree recognition during the Fifth Mexico-China Rectors' Forum in Mexico City, organized with ANUIES, SEP, SECIHTI, and CEAIE.

Higher education institutions from Mexico and China agreed to expand bilateral cooperation in artificial intelligence (AI), applied research, student mobility, and mutual recognition of academic degrees during the Fifth Mexico-China Rectors' Forum held in Mexico City. Announced in late November 2026 by the National Association of Universities and Higher Education Institutions (ANUIES), the summit builds on over 15 years of bilateral academic dialogue to align university research with national technological and industrial priorities.

"Education is a noble cause of historical value and continuous development. Both China and Mexico regard the training of qualified talent and the production of knowledge as strategic pillars for national transformation," says Chen Daojiang, Ambassador of the People's Republic of China to Mexico, in remarks shared during the event.

According to Luis González, Executive Secretary General, ANUIES, government-level dialogue between both nations has created new opportunities for joint research initiatives, professional training, and faculty and student exchanges. He noted that integrating artificial intelligence into higher education teaching and research methodologies, alongside strengthening university-industry linkages for applied R&D, served as central pillars of the forum.

The academic agreements reinforce broader bilateral scientific and technological frameworks established by federal agencies in 2026. As previously reported by Mexico Business News, Mexico and China signed a memorandum of understanding in September 2026 to expand cooperation across AI, supercomputing, robotics, electromobility, and technology transfer, creating institutional channels for Mexican universities and research centers to collaborate directly with Chinese academic and technological organizations.

Concurrently, Mexico has significantly scaled domestic public investment in scientific computing and applied research to modernize its higher education ecosystem. According to separate Mexico Business News coverage, the Ministry of Science, Humanities, Technology and Innovation (SECIHTI) increased project funding by 111% in 2026, adding MX$1.68 billion (US$91.8 million) across 1,340 initiatives, while launching the National High-Performance Computing and AI Cluster to connect public universities with advanced computing infrastructure.

Held following the fourth edition of the forum in Beijing in September 2023, the Mexico City gathering convened representatives from the Ministry of Public Education (SEP), SECIHTI, and the China Education Association for International Exchange (CEAIE) around three operational priorities:

Academic Mobility and Credentialing: González emphasized expanding bilateral scholarship programs, language preparation, and streamlined mutual recognition of academic credits and degrees earned at Mexican and Chinese institutions.

University-Industry Linkages: Participating rectors outlined mechanisms to connect academic laboratories with private-sector enterprises to execute applied R&D projects and expand professional internship pathways for students.

Institutional Continuity: Gustavo Pacheco, General Rector, Metropolitan Autonomous University (UAM), noted that the forum sustains more than five decades of diplomatic ties and 15 years of structured bilateral higher education cooperation, while Ambassador Chen highlighted alignment between China's educational modernization goals and Mexico's focus on public education and social equity.
